hook: SCP-1055 opens by warning that the document itself is risky to read, and it means it. The procedures describe a carefully furnished home, a teddy bear that must never leave someone's arms, and staff who are deliberately kept misinformed. Pay close attention to who is being described in each paragraph.
whyItMatters: It is a Keter whose containment problem has no clean answer, because the usual tools of documentation and staffing are part of the hazard. The file ends with notes from three O5 members, a compact way to watch the Council split over ethics and cost. Its k-class-scenario tag makes clear that the stakes are far larger than the cozy procedures suggest.
thingsToNotice:
The twist is that SCP-1055 is not Mikey but Bugsy, the teddy bear he is never allowed to put down. The real anomaly is a grizzly-like mass that grows with every person aware of it, faster when they are afraid, without any known upper limit, and only shrinks if most of those people die. Mikey, a man with Down syndrome and autism, is the caretaker D-1055, and the procedures and description are written so that on-site staff believe he is the anomaly and Bugsy is just a creepy, badly sewn toy.

The backstory explains why this works: after the twelfth breach and the bombing of Site-76, he was found alone in the rubble hugging the shredded creature, and his purely protective affection does not feed it. The document also tells you, the reader, that you are now one of the people who would have to die to eliminate it. The O5 notes then sharpen the ethics: O5-10 refuses to let the world rest on a disabled man's hugs, O5-5 mockingly suggests delivering the news in person so one fewer person knows, and O5-7 reveals that more intellectually disabled people are already being recruited and groomed as replacements.
